title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-02-07
lineage: [SBD MR > C > D > CD] + [AUD MC > 4C > CD patches]

ai_review.summary: Fair matrix recording marred by early muddiness, but the show shines with a joyous Sawmill and a scorching China Cat > I Know You Rider sequence.
ai_review.review: The performance is highlighted by Jerry’s pedal‑steel on “Sawmill,” a tight “Black Peter,” and an electrifying “China Cat > I Know You Rider” stretch, while the later soundboard mix finally clears up after a muddy, monitor‑swapped first half. Recording quality is uneven – early songs suffer from mud, delayed stage‑mic switches and balance problems – but it improves enough to capture the band’s 1970 country‑flavored set.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is generally good with several standout moments, but recording issues (muddy early mix, mic switching problems) drag the overall experience down, yielding an average‑plus rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early portion is muddy and suffers from delayed stage‑mic switches (Hard to Handle, Cold Rain & Snow). Balance problems noted; later tracks become clearer soundboard mix but some cuts (Good Lovin') remain.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A single long set heavy on country covers; early songs are hampered by monitor issues, but the band builds momentum with strong mid‑set numbers before the recording quality finally steadies.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal steel on “Sawmill” is joyous; his solo work in “Uncle John's Band” shows early exploration of new ideas.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as too boomy during early songs and suffers from mic‑switch delays.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocal leads on “Seasons of My Heart”; banter with Garcia noted before “China Cat”.
